text_read: grep of the whole file for light, lamp, moon, sun, lightning, eye; read songs I. 57-ish (lines 960-990), I. 76, I. 93, II. 33 in full.
mode_evidence: 'look within, and behold how the moon-beams ... shine in you' implies inner seeing, but the poems never separate perception from metaphor; 'The moon shines in my body, but my blind eyes cannot see it'.
onset_evidence: No method for one who sees nothing: 'One day your eyes shall suddenly be opened'; the guru 'removes the veil from the eyes'. Implies grace/guru.
what_to_do_with_light: Still the mind to silence before the splendour (I. 93).
cautions: I. 76 rejects shutting eyes and ears and bodily mortification in favour of sahaj union with eyes open
interpretation: The inner light of sun and moon is the presence of the Hidden One within the body.
practice_summary: Kabir gives no technique. He points within, where moonbeams of the Hidden One shine and the unstruck music sounds; before that splendour the mind is to be stilled. Opening of the inner eye is the guru's gift, sudden and unforced. In the sahaj song he refuses sense-closure altogether: he does not shut eyes or ears but sees with eyes open and beholds the Lord's beauty everywhere.

key_passages.anchor: within, and behold how the moon-beams of that Hidden One shine
key_passages.paraphrase: Look within to see the moonbeams of the Hidden One.
key_passages.quote: Kabîr says: "It is the sport of the Unattainable One: look within, and behold how the moon-beams of that Hidden One shine in you."

key_passages.quote: I shut not my eyes, I close not my ears, I do not mortify my body; I see with eyes open and smile, and behold His beauty everywhere
